prompt: Implement Processor.drain(ch: AmqpChannel091, queue: String, count: Int64) -> List<Bytes>. Consume exactly count messages in delivery order from a real AMQP 0-9-1 queue, preserve all payload bytes (including embedded NUL and 0xff), acknowledge each successfully captured delivery, and return independent compact Bytes snapshots. Use prefetch 1; validate qos/consume/message status and propagate failures. Reject negative count before issuing broker commands; zero count returns an empty list immediately. The caller owns and closes the connection. Keep the public signature. This is a finite low-level consumer task, rather than an indefinitely running annotation listener. Acceptance provisions RabbitMQ, publishes held-out binary messages through the independent management HTTP API, invokes your consumer, checks saved byte payloads and verifies that acknowledged messages do not reappear after connection closure. A local smoke run requires a configured broker; submit provisions it automatically.
